# My plan this year

Alright, let me think through this. I'm Old Wang, 58 years old, been working these fields since I was a boy. My wife and I work the land, one son works in town at a factory, and my daughter-in-law helps when she can — so really it's mostly the two of us with some hired help during wheat and cotton harvest.

Twenty-eight mu is not a small plot, but it's not a big farm either. I can't afford to waste, but I also can't afford to cut corners on my main crops. Most of my land goes to wheat-maize — that's the bread and butter around here, and after 40 years I know how to grow it. The other crops are for family food and a little extra cash.

## Land allocation

I put most of my land — 22 mu — into wheat-maize double crop. That's been my system for decades. Then about 3 mu in cotton on the sandier plot where wheat doesn't do as well. I keep about 1.5 mu of chrysanthemum — my wife manages that, it's good cash money if prices hold. Half a mu each of soybean and mungbean in the corner plots, rotated around for the soil, mostly for home eating and giving to relatives. And about 0.6 mu of spinach near the house — we eat a lot of it, and surplus goes to the township market.

## Wheat (22 mu, winter)

I plant around October 10-15, right after I clear the maize stubble. I use Jimai 22 seed — I've been buying it at the agricultural supply shop for years, it's steady. I don't save seed for wheat anymore, the new varieties are worth buying fresh.

For fertilizer: the extension fellow says 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is enough, but I always do a bit more — about 18 kg N/mu total — because my ground has been worked hard for a long time and I'd rather waste a little money than lose yield. I put down compound fertilizer before planting (this gives me my phosphorus and potassium too, about 6 kg P₂O₅ and 5 kg K₂O per mu) and then topdress urea at jointing in March when the wheat greens up. If it looks yellow I add a bit more; if it looks good I hold back.

Irrigation — well water, metered, costs money every time the pump runs. I water three times: once before winter (dongshui) to set the crop for the cold, once at jointing when I topdress, and once at grain filling if May is dry. Four times if it's a drought year. Around 450-500 kg/mu is what I expect in a normal year.

Herbicide in early spring for the bindweed and chickweed. I don't bother with fungicide unless I see scab showing up.

## Maize (22 mu, summer)

As soon as the wheat combine leaves the field in mid-June, I'm planting maize. No time for deep tillage — just a shallow rotary pass and I drill the seed right in. Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335, whatever the shop has in good seed that year. The window between wheat and maize is maybe 5 days, sometimes less. You can't waste a day.

Fertilizer on maize — I use a compound at planting with the seeder, about 40 kg of 15-15-15 per mu (so roughly 6 kg each of N, P, K from that), then topdress urea at the big bell stage, about 20 kg urea per mu. That's another 9 kg N. Total around 15 kg N/mu. Maize eats nitrogen but I don't want to push it too hard because lodging is a real problem if the wind comes.

I usually don't irrigate maize unless July-August is really dry. Last year I watered once at tasseling. If it rains, I save the money.

Yield usually 500 kg/mu. Good year 550.

## Cotton (3 mu)

I plant cotton mid-to-late April on the sandier plot. Bt hybrid seed, buy it new each year — you can't save Bt cotton seed. About 15 kg N/mu, some phosphorus at planting. Two irrigations usually, one at squaring and one at boll setting. 

Cotton is labor. My wife and I pick it ourselves over September-October, multiple passes. Some years I hire a neighbor's daughter for a few days at peak picking. If the cotton price is bad like it was a few years ago, I'd think about dropping it, but for now 250 kg of lint per mu is worth the work.

Herbicide yes, and I spray for aphids and mirid bugs when I see them. Usually 3-4 sprays through the season.

## Chrysanthemum (1.5 mu)

Medicinal chrysanthemum — the buyers come from the herb company. Plant cuttings in April, harvest flowers in October-November. This is my wife's crop mostly. Moderate fertilizer, about 10 kg N/mu plus some manure we have from the neighbor's sheep. Needs irrigation 2-3 times in summer. Aphid spray a couple times. Labor-intensive at flower picking — we do it by hand, family only.

If prices are good this can bring 3000-4000 yuan per mu, much better than grain. But prices swing, and some years the buyer offers so little I'd rather feed it to the sheep.

## Soybean & mungbean (0.5 mu each)

Small plots. Plant in June. Almost no fertilizer — maybe a handful of compound at planting. These fix their own nitrogen, and frankly they're for home eating and giving to the son's family in town. Mungbean for summer drinks, soybean for tofu. I save my own seed from these. No irrigation unless it's truly dry. No spray usually.

## Spinach (0.6 mu)

I plant spinach in late August for fall harvest, and again in late September for over-winter harvest in spring. Light fertilizer, a bit of urea when it grows. Watered from the well by bucket or small hose. My wife takes bunches to market when she goes on market days. We eat a lot ourselves.

## Budget concern

Total cash input this year, I figure about 10,000-11,000 yuan. Wheat and maize take most of it. I keep some cash aside — you never know when you'll need to buy extra fertilizer or pay for an extra irrigation. My son sends money when he can, and that helps cover emergencies.
